Jinci Temple Hall of Holy Mother

Jinci Shengmudian

Built: 1032 Dynasty: Song Dynasty Location: Taiyuan, Shanxi Admission: 80 CNY Time needed: 2-3 hrs

Honest note: Complex has many later additions. Focus on the main hall only.

Basis: 1961 NPU — click Authenticity Labels to understand our classification system.

Why Visit

Earliest surviving major Song timber hall. Intricate wood-carved dragons wrap around the front columns.

How to Get There

Jinci Temple (晋祠) is 25km southwest of Taiyuan city center. Fly into Taiyuan Wusu Airport (TYN, 15km southeast of city). From Taiyuan: Bus 308 from Taiyuan Railway Station to Jinci Gongyuan (晋祠公园) -- 60 min, 2 CNY, departs every 15 min. Bus 804 from Taiyuan South Railway Station (太原南站) -- also 60 min, 2 CNY. Taxi from Taiyuan city center: 40 min (60-80 CNY). From Taiyuan South HSR Station: 35 min by taxi (50 CNY). The temple complex is easy to find -- the main gate faces the main road and the park entrance is large and well-marked. Free electric carts shuttle visitors from the outer park gate to the temple entrance (500m).

Where to Stay

Stay in Taiyuan city. Pullman Taiyuan (500 CNY/night, near Wuyi Square and Liuxiang shopping street, best upscale); Taiyuan Wanda Realm (400 CNY/night, connected to a large shopping mall with restaurants); Jinjiang Inn Taiyuan Fu Xi Jie (150 CNY/night, clean budget chain, 10 min walk to Food Street). The temple area has no hotels -- it is a suburban park setting. Plan a morning departure (8am) from your Taiyuan hotel, visit the temple (2-3 hours), return to Taiyuan for lunch. If you are visiting Foguang and Nanchan temples (the remote Tang sites), use Taiyuan as your base for 2-3 days.

What to Eat

Taiyuan is the noodle capital of Shanxi. Must-try: dao xiao mian (刀削面, knife-shaved noodles -- the cook holds a block of dough and shaves noodles directly into boiling water with a curved blade, 15-20 CNY at any noodle shop); guo you rou (过油肉, oil-braised sliced pork with black wood ear mushrooms, the classic Shanxi restaurant dish, 35-50 CNY); yang za ge (羊杂割, lamb offal soup with vermicelli noodles, a Taiyuan breakfast staple, 15-20 CNY at morning street stalls); lao chen cu (老陈醋, aged Shanxi vinegar -- visit the Donghu Vinegar Culture Museum 东湖醋园 near the railway station, free, fascinating tour of 600-year-old vinegar vats, 20 min). Taiyuan Mianshi Guan (太原面食馆) on Jiefang Road -- order the noodle tasting platter (面食套餐) with 8-10 different noodle types, 60-80 CNY/person. Food Street (食品街 Shipin Jie) near Liuxiang has 50+ restaurants and food stalls.

Best Time to Visit

Spring (April-May): 12-25C, peach and plum blossoms in the temple gardens -- this is the most beautiful season, especially late April when the Nanlao Spring-fed ponds reflect pink blossoms. Autumn (September-October): 10-22C, ancient cypress trees contrast with autumn foliage. Summer (June-August): 25-35C, but the temple complex is shaded by 1,000+ year old cypress trees (some planted in the Zhou Dynasty, now 3,000+ years old and still alive) -- surprisingly cool. Winter: -5 to 5C, the temple with snow is serene but cold. Hours: 8am-5:30pm (summer), 8:30am-5pm (winter). Admission: 80 CNY (peak season), 60 CNY (off-peak). Go early (8-9am) to experience the temple before tour groups arrive from Taiyuan.

Tips for Foreign Travelers

The Hall of the Holy Mother (Shengmudian, 圣母殿) is the jewel -- built 1032, it is the earliest surviving major Song dynasty timber hall. The eight carved wooden dragons wrapping around the front columns are UNIQUE in surviving Chinese architecture -- no other building from any period has this feature. They are not separate pieces but carved into the columns themselves. Also: the Nanlao Spring (难老泉), one of China's most celebrated springs, feeds a series of pools through the temple complex; the Zhou Dynasty Cypress (周柏, 3,000+ years old, leaning at 45 degrees against a younger tree); the 40 life-size painted clay statues of palace ladies inside the Hall of Holy Mother (Song dynasty originals). The temple complex has many Ming-Qing additions -- focus your time on the Song core (Hall of Holy Mother, Flying Bridge, and Offerings Hall). Combine with: Shanxi Museum (山西博物院) in Taiyuan (free, 2 hours, excellent Neolithic-to-Tang exhibits that provide context for Jinci), and if time: Shuangta Temple (双塔寺, Twin Pagodas, Ming dynasty, 30 CNY, in southeastern Taiyuan).
